主要内容: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has charged Ares Management LLC, a Los Angeles-based private equity firm, with compliance failures. The firm agreed to pay a $1 million penalty to settle the charges, which allege that it failed to implement and enforce policies to prevent the misuse of material nonpublic information. The SEC’s order highlights that in 2016, Ares invested several hundred million dollars in a public company, allowing it to appoint a senior employee to the company’s board. The firm’s compliance policies did not address the risks of an employee serving on the board while participating in trading decisions. Ares obtained material nonpublic information about the company, including changes in senior management and hedging strategies, and purchased over 1 million shares, representing 17% of the publicly available shares. The SEC found that Ares did not require its compliance staff to sufficiently inquire and document whether the board representative had access to material nonpublic information. The order cites violations of Sections 204A and 206(4) of the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 and Rule 206(4)-7. Ares consented to a cease-and-desist order, a censure, and the $1 million penalty without admitting or denying the findings.
